# CANDIDATE: GARTLEY_VWAP_REVERSAL

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A completed Gartley harmonic pattern near VWAP with RSI divergence signals a high-probability mean-reversion bounce. The pattern's geometric completion at point D (0.786 XA retracement) within 0.5% of the session VWAP, combined with bullish/bearish RSI divergence, provides a confluence of price structure and momentum exhaustion that precedes a reversal.

## Mechanism

Entry: Scan 5-minute bars for a completed bullish Gartley (X-A-B-C-D) where point D lies at 0.786 Fibonacci retracement of XA and is within 0.5% of the session VWAP. Simultaneously require bullish RSI(14) divergence over the last 5 bars (price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low). Enter long at the close of the D bar. For bearish Gartley (inverse) near VWAP with bearish RSI divergence (price higher high, RSI lower high), enter short at the D bar close. Exit: initial stop placed at the X point of the pattern (or 0.5% beyond D opposite the trade direction). Profit target set at 1.5R (risk-reward) or exit when price crosses VWAP in the opposite direction. Additional regime filters: only consider trades when VIX < 25 and time between 11:00-15:00 ET; avoid first/last 30 minutes.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The strategy assumes a minimum account size of $25K to trade the suggested qty of 28 contracts (based on typical 0DTE put premium ~$1.00–$2.00). A $1K paper account would realize approximately 14% of headline P&L due to position‑size scaling.
2. **Sample bias:** The hypothesis is derived from visual inspection of a limited number of historical charts (approximately 20 manually identified Gartley completions near VWAP). This small sample introduces significant over‑fit risk; the pattern may not hold out‑of‑sample.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk‑forward held‑out window has been evaluated yet).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic OPRA fill simulation has been run on the top‑3 J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst‑case scenario occurs when the Gartley completes but price continues in the direction of the prevailing trend, triggering the stop at X. A sequence of consecutive losing days could produce a drawdown exceeding 30% of equity. In low‑VIX, trending regimes the pattern may fail repeatedly, leading to negative expectancy.
6. **Concentration:** Without a backtest we cannot quantify concentration; however, harmonic patterns are rare, so if the strategy does work, a small number of days could contribute a large fraction of P&L. This will be measured post‑backtest.
